load.cpu_job: Repeated hashlib.sha256 of bytes followed by repetition of the digest; multiprocessing fork workers, terminated and joined after the loop.
load.initial_runner: The baseline loops used inline Python with the same subprocess commands and CPU job. The committed runner also validates the listing and executed test count so an incorrect filter cannot pass silently.

root_causes.cause: The harness waited for with_ready_hosts, but serve::start invokes that callback before starting the event reader/engine and publishing Phase::Ready. Routes could bind in the meantime and tool requests received module_warming. HELLO_ACK and the callback are not protocol readiness barriers.
root_causes.fix: After the host-setup callback, wait for a control-channel HealthCheck response with status ok before returning Live. The original 180-second timeout covers both setup and protocol readiness. No sleep, request retry, deadline increase, or product-code change.

root_causes.cause: FakeBroca exposes a key during send, before the host releases its per-call dispatch lock. The host also polls at dispatch_committed. The fixture could mark the fake completed while that initial poll held the lock after reading an active result; its one completion poll skipped the locked call. FakeBroca has no streaming wakeup to schedule another poll, so Fixture::delivery timed out. Waiting for key visibility, handle persistence, or watch installation would not guarantee the initial poll released its lock.
root_causes.source: crates/basal-host/src/broca/mod.rs: dispatch_model, poll, dispatch_committed; crates/basal-host/src/broca/fake.rs: send, set; crates/basal-core/src/codemode/supervisor.rs: dispatch_model
root_causes.fix: A test-only delegating Host sends the call position through a channel after BrocaHost::dispatch_committed returns. finish_usage receives that position before marking the fake run finished and doing its completion poll. The existing 10-second timeout and budget assertions are unchanged.

runs.note: Seven failed runs exited 101; two aborted after the held-action test did not reach a core open and its cleanup hit a poisoned mutex. No such failure occurred with the readiness barrier.
